verses.text: “Listen to me, you who chase after what's right and look for the LORD. Look back at the rock you were cut from and the quarry you came out of.
Look back to Abraham your father and Sarah who gave birth to you. When I called him he was just one man. I blessed him and made him into many.
The LORD has comforted Zion and all her ruined places. He's made her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the LORD's garden. There'll be joy and gladness there, thanks and the sound of singing.
“Listen to me, my people. Hear me, my nation. Teaching will go out from me, and I'll make my justice a light for the peoples.
My righteousness is close. My salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me and trust my strength.

Look up at the heavens and down at the earth. The heavens will disappear like smoke, and the earth will wear out like clothes. The people who live there will die too, but my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness won't be wiped out.
“Listen to me, you who know what's right, you who carry my teaching in your heart. Don't be scared when people mock you or let their insults shake you.
Moths will eat them up like old clothes, and worms will eat them like wool. My righteousness will last forever, and my salvation for every generation.”
Wake up, wake up, arm of the LORD! Put on your strength! Wake up like in the old days, the generations long ago. Weren't you the one who cut Rahab to pieces and pierced the monster?
Weren't you the one who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, and made a road across its depths for the people you redeemed?
Those the LORD bought back will return, singing as they come to Zion. Joy that never ends will crown their heads. Gladness and joy will be theirs, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
“I'm the one who comforts you. Who are you to be scared of people who are going to die, human beings who'll wither like grass?

Have you forgotten the LORD who made you, stretched out the heavens, and laid the earth's foundations? Are you scared all day of the oppressor's rage when he gets ready to destroy? Where's all that rage now?
The prisoner in exile will be set free soon. He won't die and go down into the pit, and his bread won't run out.
I'm the LORD your God, the one who stirs up the sea till its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is my name.
I've put my words in your mouth and covered you in the shadow of my hand, so I can set the heavens in place, lay the earth's foundations, and say to Zion, ‘You're my people.’”
Wake up, wake up! Get on your feet, Jerusalem! You drank the cup of the LORD's anger from his own hand. You drank the bowl that made you stagger and drained it to the last drop.
Of all the sons she gave birth to, there's nobody to guide her. Of all the children she raised, nobody takes her hand.
You've been hit twice. Who's going to grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, hunger and the sword. How can I comfort you?
Your children have collapsed at every street corner like antelopes caught in a net. They've had their fill of the LORD's anger, the rebuke of your God.
So listen to this, you who've been crushed and are staggering like you're drunk, though you haven't had wine.
The Lord GOD, your God who argues the case of his people, says, “Look, I've taken the cup that made you stagger out of your hand, the bowl filled with my anger. You'll never drink from it again.
I'll put it in the hands of the people who crushed you, who told you, ‘Get down so we can walk over you.’ You flattened your back like the ground, like a street for people to walk across.”
